Smart Calendar App (Dribbble shot)

A 2020 Dribbble concept for a calendar app in candy colors, cited in the article that named the style.

Source
Dribbble
Creator
Ghani Pradita for Paperpillar
Made
2020 (the screens show August 2020; cited by Malewicz in November 2020)
Style
Glassmorphism (concept; agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Playful, airy, luminous
Evidence
Inspected the shot image named in the page’s structured data (1600 × 1200, Dribbble CDN) in a scratchpad copy. Not stored. The page was read in Claude in Chrome; the cookie banner was not accepted. The exact post date was not visible on the page.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The Dribbble description reads “Calendar App exploration using some candy colors.” The shot is credited to Ghani Pradita for Paperpillar. Dribbble.

Malewicz calls it “a clear representation of this trend” and notes that it “may be on the verge of readability in some places”. Malewicz 2020.

Observed

  • The background is a soft glow of coral pink at the top fading into lilac at the upper right and white at the bottom.
  • Three tall phone screens are frosted panels: pink-tinted and translucent in their upper parts, near-opaque white in their lower cards.
  • Each panel and card has large rounded corners and a thin, lighter edge.
  • Colorful gradient spheres (Task, Notes, Event) sit on the third screen; the glass itself carries no imagery.
  • Text is a geometric sans-serif in dark plum. The primary buttons (‘Mulai’ and a plus button) are solid dark plum pills and discs.

Why it belongs

The shot matches all four diagnostic traits and also the ‘opaque primary action’ rule. It shows the Dribbble version of the style: presentation panels floating over a generated glow, not a real app screen.

Borrow

Use near-opaque white for reading surfaces and more transparent tinted glass for headers.

Make the one primary button solid and dark so it reads through all the glass.
